cards.explanation: The answer is His hometown. Mark 6:1 says Jesus "…came to His hometown, accompanied by His disciples." So He isn't just passing through somewhere new. He's heading to His own hometown. Home is a big deal, friends, and I think this trip is going to be a big one.

The answer is astonished. Mark 6:2 says "…many who heard Him were astonished." They were stunned enough to start asking out loud where all this came from. I bet that synagogue got LOUD with questions. Astonished is the word, friends, and it's a big one.

The answer is True. They really do ask it. Mark 6:2 has them wondering, "And how can He perform such miracles?" They're puzzling over how Jesus can do such things. Wisdom AND miracles, both on the table, friends.

The answer is carpenter. They say, "Isn’t this the carpenter, the son of Mary…" (Mark 6:3). Notice they don't even need to look Him up, because they knew His trade before they finished the sentence. That's what a hometown does to you, friends. Everybody already has your job title memorized.

The answer is that they take offense at Him. Mark 6:3 says, "And they took offense at Him." They started out astonished and ended up offended, and that's a quick turn, friends. The text doesn't tell us exactly why. It just tells us that's where the crowd lands.

The answer is False. Jesus is much more specific than "everywhere." Mark 6:4 says, "Only in his hometown, among his relatives, and in his own household is a prophet without honor." He names his hometown, his relatives and his own household, and the word "only" matters, friends.

The answer is that He lays hands on a few sick people and heals them. Mark 6:5 says Jesus "…could not perform any miracles there, except to lay His hands on a few of the sick and heal them." So there is healing, just a few people's worth. It's a small number next to the crowd that took offense. I think those few went home glad, friends.

The answer is unbelief. Mark 6:6 says, "And He was amazed at their unbelief." Jesus Himself is amazed, and that's the word the text gives us. Earlier in the passage the crowd was the one astonished, so now the amazement goes the other direction. Quite a switch, friends.

The answer is that He goes from village to village teaching. Mark 6:6 says, "And He went around from village to village, teaching the people." The hometown said no, and Jesus keeps right on teaching. He doesn't stop, friends. He just moves on to the next place.
